subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw core own automated same-product archive import/restore, or should core stay limited to safer backup export, platform conversion, verification, and manual restore guidance?
rationale: The answer determines CLI namespace, archive trust, secret/session portability, destructive write policy, and whether overlapping plugin or backup work should proceed in core.

options.title: Scope a minimal native import contract
options.body: Define a preview-first core import/export lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Prefer backup export/convert plus manual restore
options.body: Keep automated restore out of core for now and improve backup output, platform targeting, verification, and docs so users can perform migration safely without a destructive importer.

options.title: Route most capability to plugins or ClawHub
options.body: Narrow core to missing APIs and let plugin or skill packages own optional cloud, scheduled, encrypted, or workspace-specific migration flows.

recommendation.title: Scope a minimal native import contract
recommendation.body: Define a preview-first core import/export lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior implementation discussion already raised the restore security boundary concern, and this choice centers on backup/import safety semantics.
